messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: POC trial planning & workload intake — FinanceX

Hi Oliver — great chat today, thanks for walking through your main use cases. Per our call, want to capture next steps for the POC / trial and get a quick workload intake so Marissa and Dylan can size the environment and propose a plan.

High-level asks (can reply inline):
- Success criteria: what would a successful POC look like (metrics, feature acceptance, business KPIs)?
- Evaluation plan & timeline: target start date, length of trial, any blackout windows for your team.
- Workload profile: steady RPS, expected concurrency, average/peak token lengths (prompt + response), burst/spike patterns, important percentiles (p50/p95/p99).
- Ownership: primary contacts for engineering, security/compliance, and procurement.

I've attached a quick workload_template.csv you can fill (simple rows for endpoint, avg_tok, p95_tok, steady_rps, peak_rps, concurrency). If easier, paste numbers in reply. Once we have this, Dylan will propose infra config and Marissa will map the test plan and success criteria.

Attachments: workload_template.csv

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | (415) 555-0182

From: Oliver Chen <oliver.chen@financex.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@financex.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Mar 2026 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC trial planning & workload intake — FinanceX

Thanks Ben — good talk. Quick answers below and I attached a draft workload profile (financex_workload_profile.csv).

- Success criteria:
  * Functional: model covers our top 3 intent flows (invoice extraction, vendor normalization, quick QA) with >92% accuracy on our validation set.
  * Performance: 95th percentile latency for typical user prompts under 200ms and <2s for long extraction jobs.
  * Cost: unit token cost <= our target threshold (we'll share a target in a separate doc).
- Timeline: would like to start the POC week of Mar 22, duration 4 weeks with a success review in the week of Apr 19.
- Workload profile (rough): steady 20 RPS for API reads, concurrency ~10, average prompt tokens ~120, avg response tokens ~400. We have scheduled batch runs that spike to ~200 RPS for short windows (3–8 minutes) once per day for nightly processing.
- Ownership:
  * Oliver Chen — Product (POC owner)
  * Sarah Kim — Engineering (integration lead)
  * Procurement: I loop in procurement if we move to pilot/contract stage.

See attached CSV for endpoint breakdown. Happy for Marissa/Dylan to reach out to Sarah for integration details.

Attachments: financex_workload_profile.csv

Best,
Oliver
Head of Platform Product | FinanceX Solutions
oliver.chen@financex.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Chen <oliver.chen@financex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC trial planning & workload intake — FinanceX

Perfect — thanks for the quick numbers, Oliver. Looping in our POC team: Marissa (CS) and Dylan (Solutions Eng) to coordinate scope and infra sizing.

Proposed POC / evaluation plan (draft):
1) Week 0 (prep): exchange test credentials & data subset; finalize success criteria and test cases; baseline metrics. (Owners: Oliver/Sarah + Marissa)
2) Week 1–2 (integration + smoke): integration with your dev/test environment, run synthetic traffic at steady RPS to validate latency and correctness. (Owner: Dylan + Sarah)
3) Week 3 (stress + spike tests): run daily spikes to validate autoscale and sustained throughput; run extraction/long-response tests for edge-case latency. (Owner: Dylan + Marissa)
4) Week 4 (validation & handoff): collect logs, run evaluation scripts against your validation set, produce success report. (Owner: Marissa + Oliver)

Open items for Oliver/Sarah:
- Can you confirm the nightly batch spike pattern: is it always ~200 RPS for 3–8 minutes? Any weekdays vs weekends differences?
- For long extraction jobs you noted ~400 response tokens avg — do you have 99th percentile token counts for these jobs?
- Are there any data handling or redaction requirements for the test corpus?

We'll prepare a POC plan PDF (technical runbook + monitoring checklist) and share the Doc link. Dylan — can you size an initial config based on the attached CSV and Oliver's numbers and share by EOD Monday?

Thanks —
Ben

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Chen <oliver.chen@financex.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 08:12:00 -0700

Hi Oliver — thanks for the profile. I've drafted a short POC plan and runbook attached as poc_plan.pdf and a shared folder with test artifact templates here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0AExampleDrive/financex-poc

Key things on our side:
- Test harness: we will provide a small harness that replays your CSV endpoints with configurable RPS and spike profiles. We'll run with the same validation set you referenced for accuracy checks.
- Monitoring: we will collect per-route latency histograms, per-token usage, and error rates; we'll surface p50/p95/p99 in the console and share dashboards.
- Security/data: please confirm if we should treat the test corpus as production-sensitive. If yes, we'll enable stricter retention and masking in the POC environment.
- Integration checklist: API keys, allowed IPs (if you lock down egress), and sample payload formats.

If you confirm the spike cadence and any redaction needs, Dylan and I will finalize the run schedule and share the test collection commands.

Attachments: poc_plan.pdf

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

All good — confirming details so we can lock the schedule: 
- Spike pattern: yes, the nightly batch spikes roughly to 180–220 RPS for 3–8 minutes, typically at 02:00 local time weekdays. Weekends see one smaller run (~80 RPS).
- Token distribution: prompts average ~120 tokens; responses average ~400 tokens. 99th percentile for responses is ~1,600 tokens (very long extractions).
- Success criteria adjustment: 95th percentile latency < 500ms for typical prompts (we'll accept higher for the 1,600-token edge cases).
- Start date: Mar 22 (week of Mar 22) — Sarah and I will make a small test dataset available by EOD Mar 19.

Ownership recap: 
- FinanceX: Oliver (POC owner), Sarah (integration)
- Redwood: Ben (sales lead), Dylan (solutions eng), Marissa (CS lead)

We'll upload the CSV and a small sample dataset to the Drive link you shared. Looking forward to the plan.

Thanks,
Oliver
